one_line_contribution: A pre-registered audit that measures how much of an ExpeL-style experience bank's paired accuracy gain survives once a reflective prompt optimizer (GEPA) has been given the identical training episodes -- a 'substitution ratio' S -- with token-matched compiled-bank, raw-exemplar and whole-bank arms, a co-adaptation cell, and a near-duplicate positive control certifying the instrument can detect non-substitutable memory value.
closest_prior_work: The proposal nominates EvoAgentBench (2607.05202) and handles it honestly: EvoAgentBench tables ReasoningBank/Memento/GEPA on shared trajectories but has no combined cell, no token matching, no paired statistics, so the substitution quantity really is unmeasured there. The more dangerous prior work is the one the proposal never engages: the instruction-vs-demonstration ablation literature that MIPROv2 (Opsahl-Ong et al., 'Optimizing Instructions and Demonstrations for Multi-Stage LM Programs', 2024) established and that DSPy practice has replicated many times -- instruction-only vs demo-only vs joint optimization on the same trainset is exactly the 'two containers for the same training-episode information' question, with bootstrapped demonstrations standing in for the retrieved bank, and its recurring finding (demonstrations often carry more of the gain than instructions, task-dependently) is a direct prior on S. Related Work dismisses MAS-PromptBench as 'prompt optimization without memory' and otherwise treats the optimizer literature as pure methods work, never as prior evidence on substitutability. Second, Experience Distillation (2607.21051) already published the retention-ratio shape with weights as the second container, so S's conceptual form is borrowed rather than new. Third, the Skills-vs-Workflow-Memory result (2608.14036: +6.06pt matched, retrieval precision collapsing 29.6% -> 3.3%) already establishes the direction of Prediction 3; the proposal concedes this and downgrades it to 'a quantified equivalence, not a surprise', which is the correct call but leaves the compiled-arm contribution thin.
strongest_objection: S is a ratio of absolute percentage-point differences with an unmatched denominator baseline, so a high S does not identify substitution. By construction I1xM0 sits several points above I0xM0 (G2 gates on it); memory therefore has strictly fewer remaining errors available to fix at I1 than at I0, and [acc(I1xM1) - acc(I1xM0)] shrinks mechanically even under perfect, fully complementary memory value. On this scale S >= 0.6 is close to guaranteed by any optimizer run that clears G2, and Prediction 1 would be recorded as confirmed with no information having been substituted at all. Compounding this, I1 is optimized with memory absent from context, so I1xM1 is off-distribution for I1: the shrinkage measured in the numerator is interference plus ceiling compression plus substitution, and the arm that separates them (I2, optimized with the bank in context) is a secondary endpoint at 2 seeds rather than part of the primary. A reviewer will say the paper's headline -- 'published memory gains are an artifact of an un-optimized instruction' -- is not the quantity the primary endpoint estimates. A secondary version of the same problem: G1 (bank gain >= 6pt) and G2 (I1 > I0 by >= 2pt) are point-estimate go/no-go gates on n=150, while the proposal's own Measurement section reports 5-14pt re-scoring drift on small sets and a treatment-free replicate that mimicked the best real treatment; the gates are below the noise floor the same document documents.
what_would_fix_it: (a) Make a headroom-normalized S co-primary: memory's gain as a fraction of errors remaining at that instruction (error-reduction scale), plus S reported within accuracy-matched difficulty strata or with I0/I1 baselines matched by subsampling, so ceiling compression cannot masquerade as substitution. (b) Define the numerator as the best memory-fair instruction, i.e. compute S using max over {I1, I2} on the memory side rather than I1 alone, and promote I2 to 4 seeds; as written the co-adaptation cell is the only arm that fairly tests whether memory adds anything to an optimized instruction, and it is under-seeded. (c) Add the I1xC cell (see missing_baseline). (d) Bring the load-bearing agent into the track's stated 7B-32B band, or add a third in-scope agent: A1 (gpt-oss-120b) is out of the brief's model scope, A2 (Qwen3.5-27B) is pre-registered as having a null denominator, so every conclusion the paper can draw rests on one out-of-scope model and the agent-relativity framing quietly converts a generality failure into a design feature. (e) Calibrate the positive control near the effect scale -- B-dup is near-duplicate leakage of held-out test instances, an enormous effect whose detection says little about power at a realistic 3-8pt instance-specific residual; a bank with a tunable fraction of instance-specific content would give a real power curve. (f) Replace the point-estimate gates with CI-based gates or power S_dev to the declared noise floor.
missing_baseline: I1xC -- the optimized instruction combined with the compiled static bank block. The grid contains I0xC and I1xM0 and I1xM1 but never the configuration the paper's own practical recommendation implies ('compile once, pay no retrieval tokens, on top of an optimized instruction'), on E1 or E2. Without it the paper cannot say whether compilation adds anything once the instruction slot is filled, which is precisely the regime it advocates deploying. Second omission: an optimizer-selected static demonstration set (MIPROv2-style demo-only / bootstrap-fewshot, token-matched to M1). The proposal has R (unoptimized raw retrieved trajectories) and C (LLM-written prose block), so a C > M1 result is confounded between 'compiled beats retrieved' and 'prose beats exemplars'; the demonstration container needs an optimized representative, not just an unoptimized one.
preprint_collision: Among the strongest collision checks I have seen in this format: dated (2026-09-03 with a prior 2026-08-21 scan), method stated with counts (15 HF Papers queries, 244 papers, by-id verification of 54 IDs), a committed scan record, an explicit residual-risk paragraph, and -- most creditably -- it withdraws v2's central novelty sentence in light of EvoAgentBench (2607.05202) rather than defending it, and self-corrects five citations v2 wrongly retracted. That is the behavior the schema is meant to reward. Two real weaknesses remain. First, verification channel: arXiv is unreachable from the node and Semantic Scholar was rate-limited, so IDs were confirmed through web-search snippets only. That suffices to establish a paper exists, but the load-bearing novelty claim is a claim about absence inside EvoAgentBench ('contains no combined optimizer-plus-memory cell, no token matching, no paired statistics'), and an absence claim cannot be established from search snippets -- the proposal's entire remaining delta rests on a reading of a paper it apparently could not open. Second, the scan is HuggingFace-Papers-centric, which systematically under-samples arXiv-only preprints with no HF traction -- exactly where the proposal's own named residual risk lives ('a GEPA + memory ablation may exist in an appendix of a systems paper'). Finally, the check's recency calibration causes it to miss the non-preprint threat entirely: the instruction-vs-demonstration ablation results in the 2024 MIPROv2/DSPy line are indexed, not recent, and are never searched for or cited, so the check establishes freedom from recent collisions while leaving the older framing collision unexamined. No named recent preprint fully pre-empts the claim; the check is credible but not sufficient on the one absence it most needs.
